text: dsh-kb-lite 是 DeepSeek Harness 的本地知识库插件，在 Host 侧注册工具，读取 Markdown、纯文本和 PDF 文件并建立本机索引。它提供文件摄取、BM25 搜索、可选的本地向量或混合检索、原文证据问答、索引统计和按变更同步。搜索结果附带文件路径、标题、行号或页码，方便核对来源。适合希望让 DSH 检索个人文档、记忆文件或项目资料的用户。基础 BM25 无需额外服务或密钥；需要 Node.js 18+ 与 Python 3.9+，PDF 和向量检索可选安装对应 Python 库。

dsh-kb-lite adds host tools to index local Markdown, text, and PDF files for DeepSeek Harness. It offers BM25 search, optional dense or hybrid retrieval, quoted evidence, index statistics, and incremental sync. Basic BM25 needs no API key; Node.js 18+ and Python 3.9+ are required.
我想让 DSH 搜索本地的 Markdown 和文本资料
能不能把项目文档做成可检索的知识库？
让 DSH 按问题找资料并给我原文出处和行号
我有很多记忆文件，想只更新变动过的内容到索引
怎么查知识库里有哪些文件和片段？
I want DSH to search my local notes and documentation.
Can the assistant retrieve quoted passages with file and line references?
I need to refresh a local document index using only changed files.
dsh-kb-lite 的功能「文档摄取」：把 Markdown、TXT 或 PDF 文件加入本地索引；通过 kb_ingest 传入绝对路径，可递归处理目录并跳过未变化文件。
dsh-kb-lite 的功能「混合检索」：用 kb_search 搜索索引并返回排序片段、摘要和出处；可选 BM25、dense、hybrid 模式及排名权重。
dsh-kb-lite 的功能「引用证据」：用 kb_ask 按问题检索相关原文，在字符预算内返回片段、文件路径、标题、行号或 PDF 页码供回答引用。
dsh-kb-lite 的功能「增量同步」：调用 kb_sync 扫描配置的记忆目录，只摄取索引建立后变更的文件，并记录同步状态。
dsh-kb-lite 使用前须知：基础检索可离线运行；向量模型默认关闭在线下载，只有显式设置 KB_LITE_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD=1 等值才允许下载。

dsh-kb-lite README · dsh-kb-lite：Local knowledge base for DeepSeek Harness: ingest Markdown, text and PDF files, retrieve passages with BM25 or optional dense search, and hand the model citations it can point at — file, heading, line or page.

dsh-kb-lite README · dsh-kb-lite：> **0.4.11** — `kb_search` / `kb_ask` now down-weight documents whose front matter says `status: superseded` (×0.3); pass `include_superseded: true` to rank them normally. Earlier, 0.4.10 added the `orphaned` / `superseded` counts, and 0.4.4 added `kb_sync` and index-freshness reporting.

MIT. Host-only DSH plugin, six tools, no browser UI, and the engine opens no sockets. BM25 needs nothing beyond the Python standard library.

dsh-kb-lite README · Why another one：`dsh-kb-rag` is the closest existing plugin, and it cannot be installed on DSH 0.2.0-rc.2. It declares a `dsh.client.inject` entry for `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-runtime`, and that package is not part of the 0.2.0-rc.2 client baseline. It also pins `@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools` to `^0.1.0-rc.6`, which is the range DSH's own version gate rejects when the host is 0.2.0-rc.2. Every published version — 22 of them at the time of writing — carries the same peer range, so there is no older release to fall back to.

dsh-kb-lite README · Why another one：This plugin takes the other side of that trade: host-only, no client bundle, no client injection, and peer ranges written with an explicit prerelease branch so `0.2.0-rc.x` actually matches. Nothing is wrong with the idea of `dsh-kb-rag` — the blocker is the client dependency and the peer range, not the feature set. If a release appears that targets 0.2.x without injecting `dsh-client-runtime`, it will cover much of the same ground and there is no reason to prefer this one.

dsh-kb-lite README · Why another one：The scope is deliberately smaller than a full RAG stack: six tools, one local index directory, and a BM25 path that works on a machine where you have never installed torch.

dsh-kb-lite README · Features：- Six tools: `kb_ingest`, `kb_search`, `kb_ask`, `kb_stats`, `kb_sync`, `kb_clear`.
- No browser UI and no client bundle. `package.json` deliberately has no `dsh.client` field: the plugin only adds host tools, so a DSH release that changes client APIs cannot break an installed copy. That matters because a broken client half takes the whole web UI down with it — DSH starts all-or-nothing.
- Input: `.md`, `.markdown`, `.txt`, `.pdf`. PDF needs `pymupdf`; without it each PDF shows up as a per-file error and the rest of the batch still indexes. Other extensions are not read: a directory walk skips them, and a file you name explicitly is reported as `unsupported_extension`.
- Recursive directory ingest — hidden directories and `.git`, `node_modules`, `.venv`, `__pycache__` and similar are skipped. Incremental by `sha256`: unchanged files are skipped, changed files are re-indexed, `force: true` re-parses regardless. `prune: true` drops documents whose files no longer exist under the paths you pass.
- `max_files` caps one call; anything over the cap is returned as `pending` so the next call can pick it up.
- BM25 with no third-party dependency, including CJK

dsh-kb-lite README · Companion：[dsh-memory-archiver](https://github.com/imaused/dsh-memory-archiver) writes the memory files this plugin indexes: approval-free writes into memory roots, with `status: superseded` markers that `kb_search` / `kb_ask` down-weight. Each plugin works alone; install both for write + retrieval.

dsh-kb-lite README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-kb-lite
```

Or straight from GitHub:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add github:imaused/dsh-kb-lite
```

Replace `imaused` with the GitHub account that publishes the repository. Use your profile name if it is not `web` (`--profile desktop`, for example).

After it installs, restart DSH and open a **new** session. Tools are bound when a session is created; a session that was already open will not see them.

dsh-kb-lite README · Tools：| Tool | What it does | Parameters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kb_ingest` | Index files or directories | `paths`, `recursive`, `force`, `prune`, `max_files`, `with_embeddings`, `chunk_chars`, `chunk_overlap`, `kb_root` |
| `kb_search` | Return scored chunks with snippets | `query`, `top_k`, `mode` (`auto`, `bm25`, `dense`, `hybrid`), `include_superseded`, `kb_root` |
| `kb_ask` | Return verbatim passages for the model to cite, within a character budget | `query`, `top_k`, `max_chars`, `include_superseded`, `kb_root` |
| `kb_stats` | Document and chunk counts, `kb_root`, size, `updated_at`, up to 50 indexed paths, `orphaned` / `superseded` counts | `kb_root` |
| `kb_clear` | Remove the index | `confirm: true`, `kb_root` |

dsh-kb-lite README · Tools：`kb_root` is accepted by every tool and applies to that call only. Paths passed to `kb_ingest` must be absolute.

Defaults: `recursive: true`, `force: false`, `prune: false`, `max_files: 50` (clamped to 1–500), `with_embeddings: "auto"`, `top_k: 8` for `kb_search` and `5` for `kb_ask` (both clamped to 1–50), `max_chars: 6000`. `with_embeddings` accepts `"auto"` (embed when the dense stack is available), `"on"` and `"off"`; `"off"` skips vector work for that ingest when you only want BM25.

dsh-kb-lite README · Tools：`chunk_chars` (default 1200, clamped to 200–8000) and `chunk_overlap` (default 120, clamped to 0–`chunk_chars`/2) are per ingest call. The setting is stored in the manifest: changing it re-chunks every already-indexed document on the next ingest, so you do not need `force: true` for that.

dsh-kb-lite README · Quick start：These are chat prompts. Each one names the tool and the parameters explicitly, which is the most reliable way to get a deterministic call.

1. Index a documentation folder:

```
   Ingest D:/docs into the knowledge base with kb_ingest: paths ["D:/docs"], recursive: true, max_files: 50.
   ```

dsh-kb-lite README · Quick start：Expect `added`/`updated`/`skipped` counts, any per-file `errors`, and `pending` if the folder held more than 50 supported files. The path must be absolute: a relative path is not resolved against a working directory, only tried against your home directory so the error can tell you exactly what was attempted.

2. Ask a question and get citable passages:

dsh-kb-lite README · Quick start：```
   Answer from the knowledge base with kb_ask: query "how does the retry policy back off", top_k: 5, max_chars: 6000. Quote the passages and cite path and line numbers.
   ```

3. Search with BM25 only — useful for comparing modes:

```
   Use kb_search with query "BM25 k1 b", top_k: 8, mode: "bm25".
   ```

4. Check what is actually indexed:

```
   Run kb_stats and tell me the kb_root, document count, chunk count, whether dense is available, and the indexed paths.
   ```

dsh-kb-lite README · Quick start：5. Remove a scratch index:

```
   Use kb_clear with kb_root "D:/kb/scratch" and confirm: true.
   ```

This deletes the index files under that `kb_root` — `manifest.json`, `chunks.jsonl` and any vectors. Your source documents are not touched; `engine.log` stays.

dsh-kb-lite README · Configuration：| Setting | Default | Effect |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `KB_LITE_PYTHON` | not set — the plugin tries `python`, then `python3`, then `py` | Interpreter used for the engine process. Set it when the interpreter it finds is not the one that has `pymupdf` or `sentence-transformers`, or when none of those names resolves. |
| `KB_LITE_ROOT` | `~/.kb-lite` | Default `kb_root` when a call does not pass one. `~` is the user's home directory (`os.homedir()`), for example `C:/Users/you/.kb-lite` on Windows. |
| `KB_LITE_MODEL` | `BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5` | Embedding model used when dense retrieval is available. |
| `kb_root` (per call) | — | Overrides `KB_LITE_ROOT` for that one call. |

dsh-kb-lite README · Configuration：Precedence: per-call `kb_root` > `KB_LITE_ROOT` > `~/.kb-lite`.

Set the environment variables before starting DSH, not from inside a session.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：**BM25.** A pure-Python implementation, no libraries. Tokenisation is Latin words (lowercased, `[a-z0-9_]+`) plus CJK bigrams (adjacent pairs of Chinese characters) plus a single-character fallback, with `k1 = 1.2` and `b = 0.75`. This is the mode that always works: if nothing else is installed, BM25 is still a complete keyword search with ranking.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：**Dense.** When `numpy` is importable and `sentence-transformers` loads, the engine embeds chunks with `BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5` (configurable through `KB_LITE_MODEL`) and prepends the retrieval instruction `为这个句子生成表示以用于检索相关文章：` to queries, which is the convention that model was trained with. Dense retrieval finds paraphrases that share no words with the source. Vectors are produced during ingest, so an index built before you installed the extras has none — install them and re-ingest with `with_embeddings: "on"` (it backfills missing vectors even when no document changed), or with `force: true` / `kb_clear`.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：The engine **never downloads a model as a side effect of a search**: it runs with `HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1` unless you set `KB_LITE_ALLOW_DOWNLOAD=1`. Point `KB_LITE_MODEL` at a local directory (a ModelScope download works — see `tools/fetch-model-modelscope.mjs`) and dense retrieval works offline.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：**Hybrid.** Reciprocal rank fusion, `k = 60`: each retriever contributes its top `top_k * 4` candidates and the fused score decides the order. `matched_by` on each hit records whether BM25, dense, or both found it.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：`mode: "auto"` uses hybrid when dense is available and BM25 otherwise, and every result reports `mode_used`, so you never have to guess which one ran. The explicit modes degrade the same way: `dense` or `hybrid` on a machine without the stack, or on an index with no vectors, falls back to BM25 rather than failing, and says so in `mode_used`. `kb_ask` has no `mode` parameter; it picks the same way and reports `mode_used`.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：Measured on a real 45-document / 334-chunk index with 18 queries (2026-10-23): BM25 scores MRR 0.844 with Recall@3 89%, dense scores 0.861 with **Recall@3 100%**, hybrid scores 0.872 / 94%. Dense therefore earns its install even at 45 documents: the gap is exactly the paraphrase queries BM25 cannot see ("why does the plugin break the UI" against text that only says "client injection"). Its real cost is the one-off model load (~14 s): once warm, the same machine measures BM25 at ~53 ms and dense at ~77 ms per query (median over 6 queries, 358 chunks; the older ~900 ms figure amortised the first query's model load across all 18 queries). In a plugin session, `auto` answers the first query from BM25 and warms the model in the background, then upgrades to hybrid. Reranking measured *worse* on the same set (0.756): a cross-encoder promotes index-like documents that mention every keyword. `weights.rerank` exists but defaults to off. To decide for your own corpus, run the same query twice — `mode: "bm25"` and `mode: "hybrid"` — and compare the hits.

dsh-kb-lite README · How retrieval works：**Chunking** matters for citations. Markdown is split at ATX headings, and a section longer than 1200 characters is split further at blank lines or sentence ends with 120 characters of overlap. Plain text is split at blank lines and merged greedily up to 1200 characters with the same overlap. PDF text is taken page by page and split the same way, with `page` counted from 1. Every chunk records `start_line` and `end_line` — line numbers in the original file, or within the page for a PDF — which is what makes `kb_ask` output quotable.

dsh-kb-lite README · Ranking weights (0.2.0)：Every hit carries a `score_detail` object, so a ranking is never a black box:

```json
{"bm25": 23.4, "dense": 0.81, "rrf": 0.032, "source_boost": 1.4,
 "boost_rule": "memory/", "recency": 0.87, "age_days": 6.2, "final": 28.5}
```

`bm25` and `dense` are the raw per-retriever scores, `rrf` is the fused rank score, `source_boost` is the path multiplier that matched, `recency` is the time decay, and `final` is what the list is sorted by (`score` equals `final`).

dsh-kb-lite README · Ranking weights (0.2.0)：You can supply all four through the optional `weights` parameter on `kb_search` and `kb_ask`:

```json
{"bm25": 1.0, "dense": 0.6, "rrf_k": 60,
 "boost": {"memory/": 1.4, "_templates/": 0.2, "kb/README.md": 1.5},
 "recency": {"half_life_days": 30, "min": 0.25, "max": 1.0}}
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Ranking weights (0.2.0)：- `bm25` / `dense` weight each retriever. In hybrid mode they scale the RRF contributions, which is how you say "trust keywords more than embeddings".
- `boost` is a path-substring multiplier; the **longest matching pattern wins**, so a file rule beats a directory rule.
- `recency` decays a document by age: `0.5 ** (age_days / half_life_days)`, clamped to `[min, max]`. Use it when newer notes should outrank older ones — the intended setting for a memory/knowledge folder that keeps growing.
dsh-kb-lite README · Ranking weights (0.2.0)：Leave `weights` out and nothing changes; the older ranking is exactly what you get.

dsh-kb-lite README · Storage layout：Everything lives in one directory, `kb_root` (default `~/.kb-lite`, i.e. under your home directory rather than the current working directory — a desktop launch has no dependable cwd):

dsh-kb-lite README · Storage layout：`doc_id` is the first 16 hex characters of the sha1 of the normalised path; `chunk_id` is `<doc_id>:<ordinal>`. `manifest.json` and `chunks.jsonl` are plain text — you can read them, diff them, or check what was actually indexed.

dsh-kb-lite README · Storage layout：The index is derived data. Delete `kb_root` and re-ingest rather than editing these files; `kb_clear` does the delete for you. `vectors.meta.json` records the model name and width: if you change `KB_LITE_MODEL`, the old vectors are ignored (dense falls back to BM25) until you re-embed with `kb-build-dense --full` or `kb_clear` + ingest.

dsh-kb-lite README · Requirements：- **Node.js 18 or newer** — the host side of the plugin.
- **Python 3.9 or newer** — for the engine.
- **Nothing else** for BM25.
- Optional, for PDF: `pymupdf` (`pip install pymupdf`).
- Optional, for dense retrieval: `numpy` and `sentence-transformers` (`pip install numpy sentence-transformers`), in the interpreter the plugin launches (see `KB_LITE_PYTHON`).
- No database, no service, no API key.

dsh-kb-lite README · Limitations：- **No reranker.** Hybrid fuses BM25 and dense ranks; nothing re-scores the fused list afterwards.
- **No DOI or citation-link handling.** A DOI in a PDF is text like any other. `kb_ask` gives you path, line and page, not a clickable reference.
- **No Zotero (or any bibliography) import.** Point `kb_ingest` at files on disk; that is the only entry point.
- **No OCR.** A scanned PDF has no text layer, so it yields nothing. Run OCR yourself first and ingest the text.
- **No incremental vector-store update.** Every ingest rewrites the whole vector file to match the new chunk list; unchanged chunks reuse their cached embeddings, but there is no append and no background compaction.
- **The BM25 index is rebuilt per query, not cached.** That is fine for the intended size (hundreds of files, thousands of chunks) and it keeps the on-disk format trivial; it is not the design to pick for a hundred-thousand-chunk corpus. Measured on this machine: 25 chunks answer a query in milliseconds; the cost grows with the corpus, not with the query.
- **Chunk size is fixed per ingest batch.** `chunk_chars` and `chunk_overlap` are per-call; there is no per-file override,

dsh-kb-lite README · Privacy：- The engine opens **no sockets** and makes no network requests. There is no telemetry, no update check, no remote index.
- The only long-lived process it spawns is one local `python engine/kb_engine.py` per plugin instance. Before that it runs a one-shot interpreter check, described in `SECURITY.md`.
- What it reads: the files you pass to `kb_ingest`, and its own `kb_root`.
- What it writes: only inside `kb_root`.
- No credentials are read or stored. There is no key, token or account.

dsh-kb-lite README · Privacy：One caveat, because it is easy to get wrong: if you install the optional dense stack, `sentence-transformers` (not this plugin) downloads `BAAI/bge-small-zh-v1.5` from Hugging Face the first time it runs, unless the model is already in your local cache. Pre-populate the cache, or skip the dense extras, on a machine that must not egress.

`SECURITY.md` has the exact argv, the full read/write boundary, and commands you can run to check all of the above yourself.

dsh-kb-lite README · Status：Version 0.4.6. Tested on Windows 11 with DSH 0.2.0-rc.2, Node 24 and Python 3.14. Linux and macOS are untested.

How this plugin is submitted to the plugin list is written up in [docs/submission.md](docs/submission.md).

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：**A tool call fails with `python_not_found`, `python_start_failed` or `engine_dead`.** `python_not_found` means no candidate interpreter answered; `python_start_failed` means one was found but exited non-zero. Before the engine is launched, the plugin checks the candidate by running `python -c "import sys; sys.stdout.write('ok')"`, so an interpreter that exists but is broken fails here. Check the interpreter first:

```sh
python --version
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：Then point the plugin at a known-good interpreter with `KB_LITE_PYTHON` and restart DSH. On Windows, if `python` opens the Microsoft Store instead of running Python, use the real path:

```sh
KB_LITE_PYTHON=C:/Users/you/AppData/Local/Programs/Python/Python314/python.exe
```

To see whether the engine works at all, run it by hand and send one request:

```sh
echo '{"id":"1","op":"ping","params":{}}' | python engine/kb_engine.py
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：You should get a `ready` line and then `{"id":"1","ok":true,"result":{"pong":true,...}}`. If that works, the problem is the path the plugin is using, not the engine. If it does not, read `engine.log` in `kb_root`.

**PDFs are ignored or reported as errors.** PDF support needs `pymupdf` in the same interpreter:

```sh
python -c "import fitz; print(fitz.__doc__)"
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：A missing module shows up as a per-file entry in `errors[]` with code `pdf_unavailable`; the rest of the batch still indexes. A PDF that imports fine but produces zero chunks is usually a scan — there is no text layer and no OCR.

**Dense retrieval is unavailable.** `kb_stats` reports `dense: false`, and `mode: "auto"` stays on BM25. Install the extras into the interpreter named by `KB_LITE_PYTHON`:

```sh
python -m pip install numpy sentence-transformers
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：Then restart DSH. First use of the model may need the download described under Privacy. Without the stack, `mode: "dense"` and `mode: "hybrid"` silently fall back to BM25 and report `mode_used: "bm25"` — nothing breaks, but nothing dense happens either.

**The index is not where I expected.** `kb_stats` returns the `kb_root` in use. Default is `~/.kb-lite`; `KB_LITE_ROOT` or a per-call `kb_root` changes it. Pass an absolute path when in doubt.

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：**Chinese text comes back as mojibake.** On a Chinese-locale Windows console, Python's stdout defaults to GBK, not UTF-8:

```sh
python -c "import sys; print(sys.stdout.encoding)"
```

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：That printing `gbk` is normal and is exactly why the engine does not trust the console: it reconfigures its own stdin/stdout/stderr to UTF-8 at startup, and the plugin spawns it with `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` and `PYTHONUTF8=1`. Garbled text therefore means you are not talking to the engine the plugin started — check `engine.log`, and check that `KB_LITE_PYTHON` names the interpreter you think it does.

dsh-kb-lite README · Troubleshooting：**An ingest was cut short.** `max_files` stopped it. The response's `pending` count is what is left; call `kb_ingest` again on the same paths (already-indexed files are skipped by sha256, so this is cheap).
